name_note: GTDB places Clostridium scindens, whose genomes are often deposited as Lachnoclostridium or Clostridium, in the genus Clostridium_AP, a split of the classical genus Clostridium; the findings cited here concern Clostridium scindens.

sentences.text: Clostridium scindens has been described as a keystone bacterial species in the mammalian gut that, while low in abundance, has a significant impact on bile acid and steroid metabolism.
It is reported to be a commensal gut bacterium capable of forming secondary bile acids and of converting glucocorticoids to androgens.
The Hylemon-Bjorkhem pathway and the steroid-17,20-desmolase pathway have been described as first discovered in C. scindens.
Secondary bile acid formation has been reported as important in the etiology of cancers of the gastrointestinal tract and in the prevention of Clostridioides difficile infection.

A study of acute kidney injury reported that Clostridium scindens ameliorated renal dysfunction, oxidative stress and inflammation, and facilitated indole-3-acetic acid production via the tryptophan metabolic pathway.

references.title: Clostridium scindens: history and current outlook for a keystone species in the mammalian gut involved in bile acid and steroid metabolism
